caption: The drawing is a pencil sketch on a tan or light beige paper. It features a single large, vertically oriented, flaring vessel at the center, likely a decorative vase or cup. The vessel's body is adorned with floral patterns and contains three oval medallions spaced vertically: the topmost medallion features a figure (labeled "Glaube"), the bottom most medallion features another figure (labeled "Liebe"), and the central medallion shows a standing figure, possibly an angel or a classical figure, holding a cross. Around the medallions are intricately sketched flowers and leaves decorating the vessel’s surface. The rim of the vase has a thick border, and the base has a patterned, cross-hatched band. In the upper right and lower left corners of the drawing are enlarged sketches of the medallions showing additional detail, each labeled with script text: the top right labeled "Glaube" above a figure with children, and the bottom left labeled "Liebe" above a robed figure holding a child. In the lower right corner is a small schematic drawing of the vessel indicating dimensions ("3 1/3" across at the top, "81 P X" for height), showing the vessel’s side profile. The artist’s name, Richard Schoene, is written below the main drawing. The composition is balanced, with the main vessel centrally placed and supplementary drawings around the edges. The entire work is rendered in grayscale pencil.
title: Silver Beaker
